rationale: Three review lenses (blind, edge-case, acceptance) ran against the implementation diff. The edge-case lens found a critical functional bug — useIsTruncated's effect (deps: [ref], a stable object) only ever runs once, on SessionModal's very first mount, before the session loads and before the subtitle span exists; it then never re-attaches once the span mounts with real content, so the tooltip would never activate in production despite the mocked unit test passing. I reproduced this with a regression test that does not mock useIsTruncated and simulates the real loading->loaded transition (confirmed RED against the original code), then fixed it by extracting a SessionSubtitle subcomponent that mounts only once subtitle content exists, so the hook's ref attaches fresh with real content already present (matching the working Card.tsx/WorkflowCard.tsx pattern). Also addressed: tooltip target class was a hardcoded, non-instance-scoped string (now includes traceId, matching the Card.tsx/WorkflowCard.tsx convention); added a short-header regression test and a close-button-visibility-with-long-header test for the shared Popup.tsx pt.headerTitle change, since that change has a ~15+ consumer blast radius and lacked a 'normal case unaffected' check. All fixes are test-first (RED confirmed, then GREEN) and committed. Remaining minor items (exact-truncation-boundary test for the pre-existing useIsTruncated hook; the Tooltip component mounting unconditionally while data-pr-tooltip is empty) are deferred: the boundary case pre-dates this diff and is a property of a hook already used in 30+ places, and the unconditional Tooltip mount matches the codebase's existing Card.tsx precedent, not a new risk introduced here.
